text: On the highway, you're constantly searching for that elusive fastest lane. We all want to outsmart traffic, trying to shave precious minutes off our commute.
You pick one, perhaps the far left, feeling confident. For a moment, it feels right. You accelerate, believing you've chosen the perfect path.
Then, suddenly, your lane slows to a crawl. The one you just left surges ahead! Frustration builds. You wonder if you're cursed, always choosing wrong.
The truth: traffic doesn't flow in static lanes. It moves in invisible waves of congestion. These waves propagate backward, forming and dissipating across all lanes.
Your 'fastest' lane isn't about its position, but where it sits within that wave. You're not picking a static fast lane; you're just riding a dynamic, shifting pattern.
Tomorrow, you'll still drive. But now, instead of fighting individual lanes, you'll see the larger system at play. You'll understand the dance of the waves.
